goal: Create the exact candidate semantic predecessors for the first event-sourced ontology vertical in CyberAlchemy-lab before DomainSpec v2 source or Rust implementation.
goal_limits: one small Lab-native witness before legacy migration
canonical append-only typed semantic events with complete resulting subject state
one semantic event stream per ontology node or relation
one graph-wide monotonic commit cursor and ontology_at(cursor) consistent cut
separate semantic and governance streams joined by exact event identity, digest, and cursor
calculated machine state, human view, indexes, validation summaries, and snapshots
candidate meaning only; no DomainSpec source, Rust implementation, binding, conformance, migration, release, or deployment
original_intent: Make the ontology stable by making events canonical, calculating state from those events, and using DomainSpec v2 as the governed implementation method under CAV2-D65.

invariants: SemanticEvents are the canonical source for semantic ontology state.
Each OntologySubject has exactly one canonical SubjectEventStream.
Every accepted SemanticEvent has a unique GraphCommitCursor in one strict graph-wide total order.
Every SemanticEvent carries the complete ResultingSubjectState for its subject.
OntologyAtCursor returns one ConsistentOntologyCut or one ReplayFailure; it never reports partial success.
Every relation in a ConsistentOntologyCut satisfies RelationEndpointIntegrity in that same cut.
CalculatedProjection and LatestSubjectSnapshot are rebuildable and carry no independent semantic authority.
GovernanceEvent streams remain separate and join SemanticEvents only through a matching GovernanceEventReference.
Legacy ontology migration remains outside the first witness and requires a later exact owner decision.

checks.detail: All 15 required concepts have exactly one current propose disposition and one handled-definition record.
One bounded Product Capability candidate names its owner, context, outcome, inputs, output, failure ceiling, and non-authority posture.
The candidate business ontology closes over 15 concepts, 16 typed relationships, nine invariants, declared inputs, outputs, and one failure concept.

The pack and handled-definition set grant no authority, implementation, promotion, migration, publication, release, or deployment effect.

claim_ceiling: Structurally checked candidate Definition Pack for the first CyberAlchemy Lab Ontology Lifecycle witness. It proposes one Product Capability and one capability-local business ontology with 15 handled meanings and 16 relationships. It does not promote canonical definitions, accept either semantic output, authorize DomainSpec or Rust work, create a construction handoff or ConstructionBinding, prove conformance, authorize migration, publish, release, deploy, or establish a stable ontology version.
